According to Doppler's effect, whenever there is relative motion between a source of sound and listener, the apparent frequency of sound heard by the listener is different from the actual frequency of sound emitted by the source. Let S be source of sound and L the listener of sound. Let ν be the actual frequency of sound emitted by the source and λ be the actual wavelength of the sound emitted.

If v is velocity of sound in still air, then
λ=vν
If velocity of listener is vLand velocity of source is vs, then apparent frequency of sound waves heard by the listener is
ν'=v-vLv-ss×ν
Here, both source and listener are approaching each other.

Then vs is positive and vL is negative.
∴ν'=v--vLv-vs×ν=v+vLv-vsν
⇒ν'>ν
Also, λ'<λ
So, listener listens more frequency and observes less wavelength.
